section_summary: This section covers diplomatic correspondence exchanged between the Japanese Embassy in Washington, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Treasury Department between October 1939 and January 1940. The documents concern reciprocal exemption from Federal income tax under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Japanese government officials and employees stationed in or visiting the United States. Individuals covered include naval inspectors and technical officers, university professors and researchers, financial commissioners, and staff of the Japan Association for the 1939-1940 New York World's Fair and Golden Gate International Exposition.

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. that Japan grants reciprocal income tax exemptions, recommending exemption for Takeo Kimura under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.summary: Hull sends Treasury Note No. 247 of October 10, 1939 and certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) for Takeo Kimura.
subfiles.title: Certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Takeo Kimura
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges the Japanese Ambassador's request for income tax exemption for Takeo Kimura and reports its referral to U.S. tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 247 of October 10, 1939 on Kimura and says a copy went to authorities.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption for Takeo Kimura
